newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries slip in London as profit taking bites.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries slip in London as profit taking bites.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries dipped under the weight of further profit taking in London on Monday and may struggle to make much headway this week, analysts said.
They said the dollar's overnight fall against the yen had also contributed to the slide but noted the impact on the long bond had been limited.

"Taking a longer perspective, the market has had a good run over the last few weeks...and I think there will be very limited progress from here," said Dick Howard, senior economist at Julius Baer Investments in London.
"Personally, I think the market is expensive here."

By 1030 GMT, the 30-year long bond was at 97-21 to yield 6.809 percent, down from 97-28 in Tokyo and 98-01 at the New York close. The 10-year was at 100-26, yielding 6.512 percent down from 100-28 in Tokyo and 100-31 in New York.
But one trader at a U.S. bank here was slightly more optimistic about the market's prospects this week.
"We've come a long way and there's been some pull back today, but I still think there's a lot of money waiting to buy so the market's going to be well supported going forward," he said.
Howard said he still firmly believed that the Federal Reserve would have to raise interest rates at the next FOMC meeting on July 2.
"I think 5.5 percent is just a bit too low -- there's still a good chance they will raise on July 2, but that's certainly running against market sentiment at the moment," he said.
Analysts expected a fairly quiet week ahead with May retail sales on Thursday and producer prices on Friday the main figures to focus on.
The trader said swap activity was light and noted a number of shortening trades.
September T-note futures were at 111-03 in automated trade, down 4/32 from Friday. The LIFFE September contract was at 111-02, up one tick on the day.
